tldr: Successful automated code migration requires tightly integrating environment setup and interaction with code modification, forming a closed-loop multi-agent framework rather than relying solely on static analysis of code.
contributions: Analysis of current limitations in code migration workflows: over-reliance on static analysis, manual post-migration validation, and absence of dynamic feedback loops

Proposal of an environment-driven multi-agent framework consisting of a Migration Agent (M-Agent), Environment Agent (E-Agent), and Testsuite Agent (T-Agent) that creates iterative closed-loop feedback between code and environment
Exploration of challenges and future directions for automated environment interaction within code migration
methods: The authors propose a multi-agent collaborative workflow operating across four stages: migration planning, automated environment setup, test validation, and feedback refinement. The Migration Agent analyzes source code and produces migration plans and candidate code. The Environment Agent autonomously constructs reproducible build/runtime environments, captures build and runtime logs, diagnoses errors, and self-repairs configuration-level issues while routing semantic issues back to the M-Agent. The Testsuite Agent generates and repairs regression test suites, executing them within the E-Agent's environment. Failed builds or tests produce structured diagnostic feedback that drives iterative correction in a closed loop.
results: The paper is a conceptual framework paper without empirical evaluation results or benchmark numbers. It references prior work noting that LLMs cause nearly 30% of runtime errors due to poor execution outcome prediction (Cheng et al. [6]), and that ExecutionAgent correctly configured 33 out of 50 repositories across 5 programming languages [3]. No quantitative results from the proposed framework itself are reported.
limitations: Environment reproduction and dependency management remain core difficulties; accurately detecting configuration drift and inferring dependencies are unsolved challenges
Multi-agent coordination and feedback loops need more stable correction mechanisms beyond simple retrials
Industrial integration with existing CI/CD pipelines, including sandbox creation, reconstruction logging, and developer auditing, remains an open problem
The framework lacks empirical validation as no experimental results or benchmarks are reported
